full_judgment:
29. Non-examination of an independent and natural witness though available raises adverse presumption against the prosecution story. 

 30. P.W.3 Lal Chand Chowkider has admitted in his evidence that when above named five victims were taken from the house of Tajel which is also known in the locality as a police camp, 100/200 persons were present. He further admits that Relief Chairman Shafi Khan, Wajuddin, Hemchandra, Ditamber and other respectable persons of the locality were present and they saw the occurrence but the prosecution did not examine any of the witnesses. So there will be a natural presumption that had they been examined they would not have supported the prosecution case. Of course adverse inference will be drawn only if there is withholding of evidence. In the instant case it has been found that natural and independent and dis-interested witnesses have been purposely withheld: so the adverse presumption can be had against the prosecution. 

 32. The prosecution case "must be true" and not merely 'may be true'. Considered as a whole the prosecution story may be true' but between 'may be true' and 'must be true' there is inevitably a long distance to travel and the whole distance must be covered by legal, reliable, and un-impeachable evidence. It is to be borne in mind that un-certainty in evidence before the court is due to nature and quality of that evidence. In a criminal trial presumption of innocence is a principle of cardinal importance and so guilt of the accused must be proved beyond reasonable doubt. Probability however strong and suspicion however grave can never take place of proof. 

 (c) Natural in dependent and trust worthy witness though available were not examined in this case and adverse presumption is raised against prosecution case.
